Research question: "What analyses or measurements would best test whether AP-1 acts as a cellular memory mechanism?"

Propose 5 distinct, concrete ideas (analyses, measurements, or experiments) that a research lab could pursue to address this question. For each idea give a short title and a description of one or two sentences.

ideas.title: Stimulus-primed re-challenge with ATAC/CUT&RUN time course
ideas.description: Expose cells to a transient stimulus (e.g., TPA, wounding cytokines), withdraw it for days to weeks, then re-stimulate and compare transcription to naive cells. Profile chromatin accessibility and AP-1 (FOS/JUN) binding at each stage to see whether AP-1-bound sites stay open and give faster or stronger gene induction. Like the material's "crackled" and "printed" words, which keep a lasting mark, the question is whether the sites keep an imprint after the signal is gone.

ideas.title: Acute AP-1 degradation after priming to separate initiation from maintenance
ideas.description: Use degron or dominant-negative (A-FOS) tools to remove AP-1 either during priming or only after the stimulus ends but before re-challenge. If memory needs AP-1 only to establish it, the primed state will persist after depletion. If AP-1 is also needed to maintain it, the primed response will be lost. Readouts are RNA-seq, ATAC-seq and histone marks (H3K27ac, H3K4me1).

ideas.title: Single-cell multiome and live-cell reporter tracking of heritability
ideas.description: Combine scRNA/ATAC multiome with live imaging of an AP-1 activity reporter, such as a TRE-driven fluorescent protein, or endogenously tagged FOS/JUN. Follow lineages through division after a pulse to test whether the primed state passes to daughter cells and how long it lasts. Compare the cell-to-cell variability and decay kinetics with those of non-primed controls.

ideas.title: Site-specific perturbation of AP-1 motifs and chromatin state
ideas.description: Use CRISPR to mutate AP-1 motifs at selected enhancers, or use dCas9 to recruit or block them, in cells that were primed. Test whether the enhancers' memory-linked accessibility and faster re-induction depend on the motif. Pair this with dCas9-based editing of the neighboring chromatin marks to see whether AP-1 acts through those marks or independently of them.

ideas.title: In vivo lineage-tracing and tissue-repair models
ideas.description: In a mouse model such as skin wounding or inflammation, label cells that experienced AP-1 activity (e.g., with Fos-driven CreER), then give a second challenge weeks later. Compare the labeled and unlabeled cells' chromatin accessibility and response magnitude. Add AP-1 loss-of-function to show that the memory needs AP-1 and not merely correlates with it.
